# Simulated Business Overview

**What stands out:** This Pilbara iron ore operation is capital-intensive and margin-rich—EBITDA of USD 373.1M in Q1 FY2027 (80.44/t) on C1 costs of just USD 21.09/t—but vulnerable to operational shocks across a complex supply chain spanning two mines, a hub with 40 haul trucks (29 autonomous), and a single export terminal serving 6 Asian steel mills.

**Why it matters:** The three epics expose critical blind spots where SAP alone cannot connect cause to financial effect. Epic E1 (cost per tonne) requires blending SAP GL postings with OPS throughput to diagnose margin erosion. Epic E2 (predictive maintenance) demands telemetry to catch truck failures *before* they cascade into lost tonnes and higher unit costs—SAP sees only the breakdown notification afterward. Epic E3 (supplier risk) links inventory in SAP to fleet dependency and port berth utilization in OPS; a single-supplier failure can strand critical spares and halt the ship loader, costing millions per idle day.

**Next step:** Pilot Epic E2—deploy the 14-day truck failure model on the 29 autonomous haulers, cross-reference predicted downtime with spares availability in SAP MM, and quantify lost-tonne exposure to justify predictive inventory buffers.
